pr_body:
Motivation:
Write TCP and UDP packets into Pcap `OutputStream` which helps a lot in debugging.

Modification:
Added TCP and UDP Pcap writer.

Result:
Writes packets into an `OutputStream`.

Fixes #10385.
pr_comments: Can one of the admins verify this patch?

\cc @normanmaurer 

Need some help in the TCP part.

Tons of error in TCP in Wireshark.

![Screenshot (137)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24762260/91020242-db844c80-e60f-11ea-89c3-482be1aacc5e.png)
@Lukasa you are fancy giving this a look ?
Also we need some sort of test cases :)

> Also we need some sort of test cases :)

Working on the same! :D
@normanmaurer In meanwhile, can you check TCP? Wireshark goes crazy with wrong flags.
@hyperxpro I will have a look but most likely not before tomorrow as I need to finish some other stuff first :/

I added a UDPv4 test case. Do let me know if test case is fine so I can add more.

1 Bug = 1 Hour, haha.
@hyperxpro so you did fix the bug or not yet ?
Nope man, I tried but not working. Pcap is alright but segment number needs to be calculated correctly otherwise Wireshark will treat it as Out of order. Can you have a look?

Actually, I am not familiar with Swift code so I went with standard documentation to develop our PcapWriter. But I'll try to understand the Swift code and see. I will appreciate if you can give me some push.
I understood the segment number part. Can you help me with `channelActive` and `channelInactive` thing?

@normanmaurer Worked really hard and made it work properly. PTAL. Thanks :D

Edit: Yeah, lots of work is still pending but just wanted to catch your attention on the TCP part.
Ready for another wave of review. :p
Also, I like how the fixes were delivered as multiple individually cohesive commits. Makes it easier to review. 👍
All done. PTAL. @normanmaurer

issue_context.title: Porting WritePCAPHandler to Netty
issue_context.body:
SwiftNIO ships a very interesting handler that allows to dump bytes as PCAP files while these travel the pipeline. This is super useful for debugging. We should port it to Netty:

https://github.com/apple/swift-nio-extras/blob/master/Sources/NIOExtras/WritePCAPHandler.swift
comments: /cc @weissi @Lukasa FYI

Will the handler dump packets received on Netty directly or dumping will happen after packets are decoded?

Example: If I want to dump TLS packets using the handler, will it be possible? I don't wanna dump content decrypted from those TLS packets.
@hyperxpro depends where you put the handler in the pipeline :)
@johnou Makes sense!

👋 
Could I tackle this?
@devesh-shetty sure thing ... Let me know if you have any specific question. Basically it is just about porting the SwiftNIO code to Java :)
Will we be writing our own Pcap Writer or some third party library?
Thanks @normanmaurer - will ask questions if I'm puzzled about something.
@hyperxpro I think we can write our own... Looking at the SwiftNIO code it seems like this shouldn't be too much work for our use-case.

@normanmaurer I got some free time so thought I should give it a shot. I took a look at the SwiftNIO code and it writes TCP Flags too (FIN, ACK, SYN, etc). I'm wondering how we'll be able to do that with Java? I mean, we can't look at TCP Packet Flags without some Pcap library, AFAIK. Can you help me here?
The SwiftNIO one makes them up. 😉
@hyperxpro as @Lukasa said... these are just "dummy values".
Alright. PR incoming next week! :D
PTAL #10498

I have a question about `PcapWriteHandler`: I am looking to integrate it into Vert.x, but due to how the processing pipeline is beig built up there, `PcapWriteHandler#channelActive` does not get called which then obviously makes the whole thing fall down.
My question is whether or not it's safe for `PcapWriteHandler` to also implement `handlerAdded` in the same way that `channelActive` is implemented.

Thanks
I think it should work. Did you face any issues when using `handlerAdded`?

Some of the time the file was corrupted and wireshark could not open it.

Of course I don't know if that was because of the change I had made to add the `handlerAdded` method, or if it was something else.

That's why I wanted to get your opinion on whether you see any fundamental reason why it would work not if I add `handlerAdded`.

Using `handlerAdded` seems to work just fine.

However I have another question: Say one wants to capture information from both a server pipeline and a client pipeline and write it to the same pcap file, is that expected to work?
Asking because I got something like:

```
pcap: File has 1698373744-byte packet, bigger than maximum of 262144
```

when opening the file with Wireshark.

I assume that this is happening because of the mixing of segment numbers, right?

> I assume that this is happening because of the mixing of segment numbers, right?

Yes, that's correct. Pcap instance should not be shared with other pipelines.

Gotcha, thanks.

I'll into lifting that restriction if possible

review_comments: this doesn't look right... if we see an `IOException` here `pCapWriter` will be null and so we will fail with an NPE later on. I think what you should do is just release the `ByteBuf`, close the channel and let the exception bubble up.
Should I close the channel every time I get an exception?
not really... its more like if you not close it here we will be in an "invalid" state. Alternative you could also remove this handler and log.
Done, PTAL. :)
Is it make sense to send ctx.fireExceptionCaught(ex) after we close channel ? I think it reach only `TailContext`
We need to call `ctx.fireExceptionCaught(ex)` because an `IOException` is caught due to `OutputStream`. So we'll close the channel since `OutputStream` has errors and writing packets won't work.
Sorry maybe I miss something but I think for V6 we will have overflow here
No. it won't. This is IPv4 `0x0800` and this is IPv6 `0x86dd`.
Got it, I thought we were going to read sign short further in test.
This can just as well be `1`, right?
Yes, but we don't know how much a user is going to write into the TCP stream. On LAN, it can be up to `65535` so I set it to `65535`.
Layer 2 ethernet frames end with a CRC-32 checksum.
Captured real traffic with Wireshark. Didn't find CRC-32 in Ethernet Packet. :-| If I add CRC-32, It doesn't display in Ethernet Tab but marks it as `VSS Monitoring Ethernet trailer` in UDP packet,
Ok, weird. Maybe the docs I read are wrong. 🤷
I read the same. But adding CRC-32, at last, is giving weird results. Through the entire development, I'm focused on Wireshark usability. Wireshark didn't give any errors so hope it's correct. :p
Why this particular checksum?
Just a dummy checksum.
Payload here can be only in range 0... 65527  (short - 8),  is it right ?
The Packet Length includes UDP Header Size of 8 bytes and data payload of n bytes,
@normanmaurer Do I need to catch this `IOException` and fire 1 more `ctx.fireExceptionCaught(ex)`?
Is it possible null varargs ?
Nope, it's completely under our control.
We won't pass `null`.
Checksum is allowed to be all-zeros (except in IPv6).
Then we need to perform a check for IPv6 and add checksum. Not worth the effort TBH.
